conventions.convention: Gaussian random elements take values in a real separable Banach space with its norm Borel sigma-algebra; every continuous linear coordinate is centered normal, allowing zero variance.
H is the Hilbert completion of the covariance quotient B*/N, identified with its injective continuous image in B; its Hilbert norm differs from the ambient Banach norm.
μ_h is the law of W+h, so its density relative to μ is exp(z_h−||h||_H²/2).
The concentration function uses the full squared RKHS norm, strict approximation radius, and an open centered small ball; w₀ belongs to the Banach closure of H.
Expansion uses the closed Hilbert unit ball H₁ and compact inner measure, with Φ⁻¹(0)=−∞ and Φ⁻¹(1)=+∞.
The countable norming-family statement assumes HB and countable choice; for the zero Banach space it expressly substitutes the zero functional for norm-one functionals.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and countable choice. For a centered tight Borel Gaussian law on a real separable Banach space, w₀ in the Banach closure of H, n≥1, ε>0, C>1, exp(−Cnε²)<1/2, and φ_w₀(ε)≤nε², there is a measurable B_n with log N(3ε,B_n,||·||_B)≤6Cnε², μ(B\B_n)≤exp(−Cnε²), and μ{||W−w₀||_B<2ε}≥exp(−nε²). These are prior bounds only.
Assume AC and countable choice. For a centered tight Borel Gaussian law μ on a real separable Banach space, every Borel A and r≥0 satisfy μ_*(A+rH₁)≥Φ(Φ⁻¹(μ(A))+r).

Assume AC and countable choice. For h in the covariance RKHS of a centered Borel Gaussian random element in a real separable Banach space, the law μ_h of W+h has density exp(z_h−||h||_H²/2) relative to μ; μ_h and μ are equivalent.

Assume AC. Under the covariance/RKHS definition's hypotheses, Cℓ exists as a Bochner integral, Q is a finite positive-semidefinite bilinear form, N is its nullspace, and the induced map from the completion of B*/N to B is continuous and injective.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let W be a centered Borel Gaussian random element in a real separable Banach space B. There is a constant a>0 such that E exp(a||W||²)<∞. In particular, E||W||²<∞.
Assume AC. For a centered tight Borel Gaussian law on a real separable Banach space, the closed Hilbert unit ball H₁={h∈H:||h||_H≤1} is compact in the Banach norm.
Assume AC and countable choice. For a centered tight Borel Gaussian law μ on a real separable Banach space, supp μ equals the Banach-norm closure of its covariance RKHS.
Assume AC. For standard Gaussian measure γ_d on R^d, d≥1, every Borel A and r≥0 satisfy γ_d,*(A+rB₂^d)≥Φ(Φ⁻¹(γ_d(A))+r), using compact inner measure and endpoint inverse-CDF conventions.
On a separable Banach space, Borel probabilities with equal finite-dimensional pushforwards under every finite subfamily of a given countable norming family are equal.

concerns.concern: The Example specifies only T=ℕ and k(i,j)=1_{i=j}, then asserts: “The cylinder Gaussian process with this kernel has independent N(0,1) coordinates”. No mean function or centering hypothesis is specified there. The cited existence theorem takes both m and k; for example m(i)=1 with this same kernel gives independent N(1,1) coordinates. The Verification assumes independent standard normals, but that assumption does not follow from the Example as written.

alerts.finding: In lem-tight-borel-gaussian-law-has-separable-support, step 2.1 says: “The same map W is Borel as an E-valued map because the Borel sets of E are intersections of E with Borel sets of B.” The construction proves only μ(E)=1, so the original W can take values outside E on a nonempty measurable null event. For example, on a complete probability space let W=0 off one null singleton and W=v≠0 on that singleton; its law is δ₀ and all scalar coordinates are degenerate centered normal. The proof permits K_m={0}, hence E={0}, but this same W is not E-valued. An almost-sure modification is needed to justify the asserted E-valued random element.

seams_checked.note: The incoming supplier constructs cylinder laws from both a mean function and a PSD kernel and expressly disclaims Banach-valued regularity. Both pages preserve that distinction. The cylinder example's omitted mean is recorded separately as an owned concern.
